topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's focus on the molecular and cellular mechanisms governing the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Pathogen and damage recognition by pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects microbes and tissue damage using molecular patterns and diverse pattern recognition receptor pathways.

topics.label: Sentinel cell signaling, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic inflammatory consequences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated sentinel cells direct immune cell recruitment to tissues and lymph nodes, as well as the physiological hazards of excessive systemic inflammation.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammatory states
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how acute inflammation is brought to a stop, how damaged tissue is repaired, and why persistent stimuli lead to chronic inflammation or granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture closing and preview of next topic
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and announces that the following lecture will cover the complement system.
